t: Maximize Amount After Two Days of Conversions — Two Relaxation Passes
o: Start with 1.0 of initialCurrency. Day 1 lets you convert arbitrarily along pairs1 (both directions, inverse rates); day 2 along pairs2; maximize final holdings of initialCurrency. The graphs are tiny (<= 10 edges) and contradiction-free, so the optimum is separable: compute the best multiplier from initialCurrency to every currency c on day 1, and the best multiplier from c back to initialCurrency on day 2; the answer is max over c of the product. Example 1: EUR->USD->JPY (x6) then JPY->USD->CHF->EUR (x120) = 720.
k: Days are independent: answer = max_c bestDay1(initial -> c) * bestDay2(c -> initial).
'Best c -> initial on day 2' equals 'best initial -> c on the reversed day-2 graph', so one relaxation routine serves both directions.
Since rates compound multiplicatively and graphs are tiny, repeated Bellman-Ford-style relaxation until fixpoint is simplest and safe.

a.i: Build an adjacency map with both directions (rate and 1/rate). Relax all edges repeatedly until no distance improves, starting from {initial: 1.0}. Run it on day 1's graph for forward multipliers and on the reversed day-2 graph for return multipliers, then combine.
s: build(pairs, rates, rev): adjacency list with (neighbor, rate) and (neighbor, 1/rate), swapping endpoints if rev.
best(g, src): dist = {src: 1.0}; loop relaxing dist[u]*rate > dist[v] until stable.
answer = max over c in dist1 of dist1[c] * bestBack.get(c, 0.0).
a.t: O((n+m)^2) — each relaxation round is O(edges) and there are at most O(vertices) productive rounds on these tiny graphs.
a.sp: O(n+m) — adjacency maps and distance maps.

a.n: Approach 2: Memoized DFS on the DAGs
a.i: The problem guarantees acyclic conversion graphs, so the best multiplier is a longest-path product computable with memoized recursion: fwd(c) = max(1, max over incoming edges (a -> c) of fwd(a)*rate), and bwd(c) = max(1, max over outgoing edges (c -> b) of bwd(b)*rate). Combine as before.
s: Memoized fwd over day-1 edges reversed into c; base value 1.0 at initialCurrency.
Memoized bwd over day-2 edges leaving c; base 1.0 at initialCurrency.
a.t: O(n + m) — each currency is memoized once; edge scans are linear.
a.sp: O(n + m) — graphs and memo tables.

w: The relaxation version is safer in interviews because it does not rely on the acyclicity guarantee; the DFS version is elegant when the DAG promise is quoted. Pitfalls: forgetting the implicit 'do nothing' option (always worth 1.0, captured by initializing at initialCurrency), currencies absent from day 2 (multiplier 0 for returning), and floating-point comparison tolerance (use strict > on these well-conditioned inputs). Follow-up: what if rates could create arbitrage cycles? Then day-wise maximization becomes a longest-product-path problem needing detection of positive cycles.
